text.p: Malaysia's national car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd (Proton) reported a net profit on Friday of 741.47 million ringgit ($294.8 million), doubling the previous year's 355.88 million.

The profit for the year ended March 31, 1997, was slightly higher than the market consensus forecast of 713 million ringgit. Proton's pretax profit breached the one-billion ringgit mark for the first time.
The maker of the popular Proton cars reported profit before tax of 1.03 billion ringgit against 454.58 million last year. Turnover jumped 20.4 percent to 6.22 billion ringgit from 5.17 billion.
Proton said in a statement the profit surge was due to increased sales volume, productivity improvements and cost reductions.

"Sales of Proton vehicles continue to be encouraging in the light of the steady economic growth registered by the country," it said. "Ongoing efforts towards component cost reduction and improvement in prductivity will contribute favourably to the earnings of the group."
Proton chairman Saleh Sulong told reporters after releasing the results that the company achieved a "double digit decrease in costs" during the financial year.

Analysts said the company was helped by the relatively weak yen/ringgit exchange rate, especially in the second half of last year. Proton is exposed to fluctuations in the yen/ringgit rate as a large proportion of its components are imported from Japan.
Saleh said Proton's exposure to exchange rate fluctuations currently stood between 20 and 30 percent of component costs.
Proton's chief executive officer Tengku Mahaleel Tengku Ariff added that around 80 percent of the components of Proton's engines were now sourced locally.
"They were helped by the yen, especially in the second half," said Azizah Ahmad, auto analyst at MBf Northern Securities.
"In the first half, the yen was at 2.3 (ringgit per 100 yen). In the second half, it was at 2.11. So even though the first half was very high, the yen came down in the other six months," Azizah said.

Proton's Saleh said the company was comfortable with the current yen/ringgit trading range."We are within our budget as long as the yen stays at about these levels...unless there is a massive appreciation."
Asked how he would define a large appreciation, Saleh said: "If it was far in excess of 230 yen."
The ringgit closed a bit higher in Kuala Lumpur on Friday at around 220 yen.
Saleh also said the company had taken hedging measures against yen fluctuations.
"We have taken adequate measures in our hedging and forward contracts to ensure we will achieve our results according to our target," he said.
Proton's stock surged 90 cents or 7.1 percent to 13.60 ringgit ahead of the results as the market got wind of the strong earnings figures, dealers said.

Some analysts thought the stock could be driven higher on Monday. "How many companies can come out with such a high profit growth?" said Choo Swee Kee, auto analyst at Vickers Ballas. "It will be good for the stock. The stock has already started moving up today. It should go up a bit more on Monday."
($1=2.515 ringgit)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
